pages.aiIntro: AI reads PDFs from unfamiliar labs and medical reports, writes comments on lab results, the monthly summary and visit questions. This needs a key from one of these services (OpenRouter, ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, YandexGPT, GigaChat) or your own model on a home server.
pages.anamnesisIntro: Who the patient is, for the doctor report header. The medical background is a short account of the illness and treatment in your own words: the AI receives it with every question, so the more accurate it is, the more useful the answers.
pages.mcpIntro: Model Context Protocol lets external AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and others) read MedControl data and, if you allow it, add notes and diary entries. Off by default.
pages.protocolIntro: The protocol determines lab alerts, diary scales, marker notes and what the AI knows about the treatment.
pages.protocolAlertsIntro: When a lab marker crosses a threshold, an alert appears on Today and in Telegram.
pages.protocolNotesIntro: The text appears on the marker card in a block titled with the protocol name: for example, what the medication does to the liver.
pages.protocolScalesIntro: Which 0–3 scales to show in the diary. Recorded data is kept: if you turn a scale off, old values stay in the history and reports.
pages.protocolTexts: Name and texts for the AI
pages.serverIntro: Status of what runs on the server by itself: nightly backups and PDF reading. You usually don't need to check here: if there is a problem, you will get a Telegram message.
pages.serverIntroDesktop: Backups and PDF reading. The desktop version has no nightly backups: from time to time, save the "Full data archive" to iCloud, OneDrive or a flash drive.

serverOnly.fallback: This feature works only in the server version of MedControl.

why.appleHealth: The phone sends data to your server's internet address, and the desktop app has no such address.
why.dicom: The imaging archive needs a separate service, Orthanc, which runs only on the server. Imaging reports and lesion sizes are entered as usual.
why.backups: Nightly backups are done by a server service. In the desktop version, save the "Full data archive" to an iCloud or OneDrive folder or a flash drive.
why.passkeys: Passkeys (Face ID, Touch ID) are tied to the site address. The desktop app opens with a password.
why.egress: The proxy for AI and Telegram is a server service. The desktop app connects to the internet directly.

privacy.openrouter: Requests go only to models whose providers do not store data or train on it.

privacy.deepseek: DeepSeek's servers are in China: patient data will go there.
privacy.custom: If the model server is yours, data does not leave your network.

mcpCard.blockedText: AI agent access is turned off in this server's settings (DTC_MCP=off).
mcpCard.readFirst: Read this before turning it on.
mcpCard.warnData: An agent with a token can see the patient's medical data: labs, medications, diary, treatment history, imaging, appointments and doctors' contacts.
mcpCard.warnCloud: Data goes wherever the agent and its model run, often a cloud service (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google). Check who you are giving it to and whether the service stores requests.
mcpCard.warnToken: A token is like a password: give it only to your own apps, and do not publish or forward it. A "read and write" token can add notes and diary entries.
mcpCard.warnAudit: All access is recorded in the log on this page. Turning access on and creating new tokens send a Telegram message. Turning access off, "Sign out everywhere" and changing the password immediately revoke all tokens.
mcpCard.ack: I understand that I am giving AI agents access to medical data and that I am responsible for who gets tokens.
mcpCard.howTo: Streamable HTTP protocol, token in the Authorization: Bearer … header. The agent gets data through tools: patient profile, labs with reference ranges, medications, diary, appointments, history, imaging, contacts, search; with a write token it can also add a note and a diary entry.
mcpCard.disableConfirm: Turn off access? All tokens will be revoked.
mcpCard.freshToken: Token "{name}" is shown only once, copy it now: {token}

localeCard.timeZoneHint: Days are counted by it: dose check-offs, the diary, reminders. Change it if you move.

profileCard.title: Profile for the AI
profileCard.intro: What the model knows with every request: milestones, imaging with RECIST, therapy and doses, the diary for the past two weeks, open alerts. All of this is collected from MedControl automatically. Add here what MedControl doesn't have: stage, radiation regimen, other conditions, allergies, other medications.
profileCard.placeholder: For example: diagnosis and stage, surgery (year), radiation therapy (dose). Other conditions and regular medications.
profileCard.needsAi: Needs the AI assistant: Settings → "AI assistant"
profileCard.draftHint: The model rewrote the medical background from milestones, imaging, therapy and labs. Read the "What changed" section and the discrepancies at the end. The current text stays untouched until you accept.
profileCard.truncated: The response was cut off by length: the end of the text is lost. Request it again or shorten the medical background.
profileCard.diffHint: How the current text differs from this version: added in green ({added, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}), removed in red ({removed}).

telegramCard.title: Telegram reminders
telegramCard.desktopWarning: In the desktop version, the bot and reminders work only while the app is open and the computer is awake.
telegramCard.whatComes: A dose reminder at {dose} if the dose isn't checked off; every new alert from labs and the diary; on Mondays, a notice if there have been no labs for {days} days.
telegramCard.whatComesAgain: A dose reminder at {dose} if the dose isn't checked off, and a repeat at {again}; every new alert from labs and the diary; on Mondays, a notice if there have been no labs for {days} days.
telegramCard.botUsage: You can send the bot lab PDFs (it reads and saves them) and a diary entry in one line: "pressure 135/85, fatigue 2, weight 71, wellbeing 4".
telegramCard.step1: In Telegram, open @BotFather, use the /newbot command, copy the bot token and paste it here.
telegramCard.step2: Send your bot any message and press "Find chat".
telegramCard.noChats: No chats found. Send the bot a message and press "Find chat" again.
telegramCard.chatConnected: Done, the bot is connected. Press "Send test".
telegramCard.tokenReplaced: Token replaced. Find the chat again.
telegramCard.tokenFromAdmin: The bot token is set by the server administrator.
telegramCard.passwordHint: The bot and the chat receive reminders and security messages, so this change is confirmed with the password.

backupCard.title: Backups
backupCard.sameDisk: Backups are on the same drive as the data: if it fails, they are lost too. Connect a second drive (MIRROR_DIR) or an encrypted cloud: docs/OPERATIONS.md, "Backups".
backupCard.noReport: The backup service hasn't reported yet. The first line will appear tonight at 3:30 AM.
backupCard.how: Three tiers: a nightly dump on the server, a copy to a second drive, an encrypted copy to the cloud. On Sundays the dump is restored to a test database and verified. At 8:30 AM a line comes in Telegram, and if there is a problem, an alert at 9:30 AM. How to restore: docs/RESTORE.md.

importCard.title: Load archive
importCard.done: Archive loaded: {tables}; files: {files}. <home>Go to the home screen</home>
importCard.notEmpty: An archive can be loaded only into a new install with no records yet, so it does not mix or overwrite anything. This install already has records.
importCard.intro: Moving to another computer, from the server to the desktop version and back, restoring from your own copy. All records, files, the medical background, the treatment protocol and personal settings are transferred. Sign-in, password, AI keys, Telegram and agent access stay as set up here.
importCard.slow: A large archive takes several minutes to load. Do not close the page.

reminderTimes.title: When to remind
reminderTimes.hint: For the main medication: a reminder if the dose isn't checked off, and a repeat in the evening until all of the day's doses are checked off. Supportive medications have their own time, on the medication card. Times follow the time zone from "Language and region". The notice about old labs comes on Mondays.

recoveryCard.title: Password recovery code
recoveryCard.created: Created {date}. If the code is lost or someone else may have seen it, create a new one: the previous one will stop working.
recoveryCard.createdFirstRun: Created at first launch. If the code is lost or someone else may have seen it, create a new one: the previous one will stop working.
recoveryCard.none: No code: if you forget your password, you will not be able to regain access. Create a code and write it down.

recoveryCode.file:
MedControl password recovery code

{code}

Created {date}. On the sign-in screen: "Forgot password?", this code and a new password.
After a password reset a new code is issued, and this one stops working.
Keep it away from your computer: on paper or in a password manager.
recoveryCode.warning: Password recovery code. If you forget your password, press "Forgot password?" on the sign-in screen and enter this code. There is no other way to regain access: there is no email recovery, and the data is stored only with you. The code is shown once.
recoveryCode.keepApart: The code opens sign-in in place of the password and passkey (Face ID), so keep it away from your phone and computer: on paper or in a password manager.

labsParsersCard.title: Labs
labsParsersCard.intro: PDFs from these labs are read right away, without AI and without being sent anywhere. Lab reports from other labs are read by the model (an AI key is needed), and you check the lines before saving. Scans too: a service that can see images reads them itself; for the others, the text is first recognized right in MedControl.
labsParsersCard.down: Python PDF parsing is on (PDF_ENGINE=python), and the service returned an error: check docker compose ps ingestion.

exportCard.intro: One ZIP with everything: tables in JSON, lab results as a single CSV table, the medical background, all uploaded files. For your own archive and for moving to another system. The archive is not encrypted: store it the way you store medical documents.
